# Agent HUD

A local dashboard for the skills and plugins scattered across a coding agent
setup. Free, macOS only for now, MIT license, no account.

## What it does

Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor load the name and
description of every installed skill into the model's context at the start
of a session, whether that session uses the skill or not. Agent HUD shows
how many skills a selected project loads, and lets you save the plugins and
skills you use together as a group and apply a different group per project.
It reads and writes settings files on the machine it runs on and needs no
account. On its own it makes one request, a GitHub Releases check once a
day for update notices; a Homebrew install can also update itself when the
user clicks Update now, and then Homebrew does the download.

## Links

- Homepage (English): https://ganggangstone.github.io/agent-hud/
- Homepage (Korean): https://ganggangstone.github.io/agent-hud/ko/
- Repository: https://github.com/ganggangstone/agent-hud
- Install with an AI agent: ask it to "Install Agent HUD from https://github.com/ganggangstone/agent-hud and follow the For AI agents section of its README"
- Install: `brew install --cask ganggangstone/tap/agent-hud-app` (app icon plus the `agent-hud` command), or `brew install ganggangstone/tap/agent-hud && brew services start agent-hud` for the command only (or `git clone https://github.com/ganggangstone/agent-hud.git && cd agent-hud && ./install.sh`)
- Design decisions: https://github.com/ganggangstone/agent-hud/blob/main/docs/ADR.md

## Summary

- Price: free
- Platform: macOS (Linux via running `server.py` directly; Windows not supported yet)
- License: MIT
- Dependencies: none — a single Python file, standard library only
- Account: not required
- Network use: one GitHub Releases check a day; Homebrew downloads an update only when the user clicks Update now
